title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1966-05-19
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat -> Sonic Solutions -> CD

ai_review.summary: Soundboard capture of the early‑psychedelic 5/19/66 Avalon benefit show – highlights include a vibey Mindbender and the “Tastebud” track, but Garcia’s tone draws mixed opinions.
ai_review.review: The recording is a soundboard (SBD) source that delivers clear, listenable audio with no reported technical flaws. Musically the concert is a snapshot of the Dead’s early psychedelic period; reviewers praise the vibrato‑laden Mindbender and the rare “Tastebud” performance, yet some feel Jerry Garcia had not yet settled on his signature tone, making the overall show feel mixed.

ai_rating.rationale: Average star rating across eight reviews is ~4.1; most comments are positive about the recording and specific songs, but there are notable criticisms of Garcia’s tone, leading to a balanced overall score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: No complaints about clarity or mix; reviewers focus on musical aspects rather than audio flaws, indicating the SBD capture is clean and listenable.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The concert was part of a multi‑media benefit event at the Avalon, blending music with poetry and theater; set pacing is not specifically described in reviews.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Opinions diverge – one reviewer calls Garcia’s tone “indifferent,” while another defends it as typical of early ’66 playing, noting less powerful solos compared to later years.
band_member_comments.Phil: Mentioned using vibrato on vocals during Mindbender, indicating a notable contribution in that song.
